timing: The source timing boundary is represented rather than merely an eventual result.
constraint: Literal method/field/type/limit and logical modality match.
outcome: The source-required result and safety effect are both present.
version: The R1.0 source baseline and generated corpus scope agree.

| Analyst | Create cases, add attachments, request drafts, evaluate evidence, and read authorized cases/runs. Cannot approve their own high-risk recommendation. | Queue visibility, label-correction permissions, closure permission, and manual publication permission. | Source, pp. 11–12; p. 83, §A.2 |

| Auditor | Obtain immutable evidence without editing case content; inspect decision metadata, prompt-template digests, and access events within redacted scope. Read audit events. | Detailed content-redaction matrix and export rights beyond the explicit export contract. | Source, pp. 11, 62, 83 |

This specification defines data requirements for OrionDesk AI **OD-AI-DDS-001, R1.0 / revision 1.3**. It preserves identifiers from [01_screen_functions.md](01_screen_functions.md) and [02_api.md](02_api.md).

**DAT-R-001 — Confirmed:** PostgreSQL is authoritative for mutable metadata and case state; encrypted private object storage holds original and normalized artifacts; hybrid vector/keyword indexes hold nonauthoritative searchable derivatives; caches hold versioned ephemeral results with short TTLs. The orchestrator has no direct database credentials. No datastore is publicly exposed.

| DAT-002 | `workspaces` / Workspace | Policy and quota scope; domain configuration boundary | Each tenant-owned workspace belongs to a tenant; groups users, connectors and cases | SCR-007; API-028, API-050, API-056 |

Case idempotency binds **actor + request fingerprint to one outcome for 24 hours**. Namespace, expiration equality, unsuccessful/in-flight outcome retention and post-expiry behavior **Need confirmation**. Do not apply this period universally to batch deduplication.
| Model output has unknown fields, invalid citations or control-character injection | Bounded validation retries; final `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`, no publication |
| Tool-call budget exhausted, repeated invalid plans, policy denial or deadline expiry | Stop and expose exact failed checkpoint |
| `AUTO_ALLOW` | Policy outcome exists; still requires evidence and current authorization for publication | Complete eligibility predicate and auto-allow workflow path |

**ERR-R-001 — Confirmed:** Oversized uploads, prompt injection, cross-tenant identifiers, stale approvals and ungrounded recommendations fail closed with stable, non-sensitive errors. Partial processing must never appear as an approved answer. Recovery, replay and degraded operation do not bypass authorization or publication gates.

This specification defines data requirements for OrionDesk AI **OD-AI-DDS-001, R1.0 / revision 1.3**. It preserves identifiers from [01_screen_functions.md](01_screen_functions.md) and [02_api.md](02_api.md).

**DAT-R-001 — Confirmed:** PostgreSQL is authoritative for mutable metadata and case state; encrypted private object storage holds original and normalized artifacts; hybrid vector/keyword indexes hold nonauthoritative searchable derivatives; caches hold versioned ephemeral results with short TTLs. The orchestrator has no direct database credentials. No datastore is publicly exposed.

| DAT-002 | `workspaces` / Workspace | Policy and quota scope; domain configuration boundary | Each tenant-owned workspace belongs to a tenant; groups users, connectors and cases | SCR-007; API-028, API-050, API-056 |

| DAT-003 | `cases` / CaseAggregate / CaseRow | Current versioned case aggregate; Case Service | Each case belongs to one tenant and one workspace; separate attachment and run references | SCR-001–002; API-001–005 |

The source confirms batch processing, including asynchronous classification, extraction, indexing, reconciliation, retention and bounded historical backfill. `BAT-*` identifiers are assigned here because the source supplies no batch-job IDs. These identifiers identify logical functions, not mandatory separate executables, queues or deployments.
Related contracts and data identifiers refer to [02_api.md](02_api.md) and [03_data.md](03_data.md). Earlier proposed schemas and screen placements remain proposals.

| BAT-001 | Case classification — attach policy-aware labels, confidence and provenance | Classifier; Triage Agent classifies cases; exact component relationship Needs confirmation | `CaseCreated`; case creation through API-001. Separate manual rerun unspecified | Accepted case ID/revision → classification output; no confirmed attachment-readiness dependency | Source, p. 12, §2.2.1; p. 40, §11.1.1; p. 87, §C.1 |

| BAT-008 | Durable grounded AI workflow and publication validation | Orchestrator, Research Agent, Draft Agent, Model Gateway, deterministic Policy Service | API-008/API-009 run request; `AgentPlanApproved`, `WorkflowStageAdvanced`, `ApprovalDecisionRecorded` drive consumers | Authorized case, admission, approved capabilities/evidence → candidate/policy/review → gated publication or failure | Source, pp. 37–46, 48–49, 69, 87 |

| Same creation key and changed fingerprint | `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`; case test requires HTTP `409` | BR-004 |
